result.notes:
No mainstream-path differences found across 2393 harness case-pairs (5 further manual pairs run by hand). Coverage: (1) /tmp/mainstream_bounds.mjs 368/368 — every required boundary: witver 0 with program lengths 19,20,21,31,32,33 over 6 hrps ('bc','tb','test','x9','a','abcdefghijkl'); witver 1..16 with lengths 2,3,20,32,39,40,41 over 'bc' and 'ltc'; plus exhaustive length 1..42 for witver 0 and 16; plus all-0x00 and all-0xff programs at lengths 2,20,32,40 for witver 0,1,16. (2) /tmp/mainstream_rand.mjs 400/400 at SEED=12345 and 400/400 at SEED=987654321 — random hrp [a-z0-9]{1,12}, witver 0..16, program length 2..40, random bytes 0..255, with witver-0 cases biased so half hit valid length 20/32. (3) /tmp/mainstream_sweep.mjs 663/663 — dense cross product witver 0..16 x length 2..40, random bytes. (4) /tmp/mainstream_hrp.mjs 396/396 — 33 hrp shapes x 12 (witver,length) combos, deliberately including hrps that contain the '1' separator char ('1','11','a1','1a','a1b','bc1','q1q','1bc','abc1def','l1l'), all-digit hrps ('999','000000','0123456789ab'), 1-char and 12-char hrps. (5) /tmp/mainstream_fmt.mjs 166/166 — int()-accepted literal decorations on program bytes and on witver (leading/trailing space, tab/newline, '+' sign, zero padding).

Both output branches are genuinely exercised and agree: witver 0 produces an address only at program length 20 or 32 (2,19,21,33,40,41 -> "None"); witver 1..16 produces an address for lengths 2..40 and "None" at 41; witver order-of-operations (checksum computed before CHARSET lookup) needs witver>=32 to matter and is outside this assignment.

Two suspicions raised by reading the port, both CHASED AND DISPROVED — do not "fix" them: (a) /output/lib/bech32/codec.mjs:36 omits CPython bech32_decode's `len(bech) > 90` guard, but the bundled package has no cap either: `--a aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa --b 1 --c <forty 1s>` yields the same 91-char address from both, and hrp lengths 19,25,30,31,40,60,80 all round-trip identically up to 152 chars. (b) /output/lib/bech32/segwit.mjs:41 returns null when convertBits fails, whereas stock bech32 1.1.0 would raise TypeError on `[witver] + None`; the reference prints "None" rc=0 for `--a bc --b 1 --c 256,1`, matching the port, so the bundled encode has its own None guard. Also independently confirmed the port's central assumption (plain Bech32 checksum for every witness version, no Bech32m): reference emits bc1pqypqj3p230 for `--a bc --b 1 --c 1,2`.

Nothing suspicious remains unconfirmed on the mainstream success path.

mismatches.why: The reference bech32 rejects any HRP longer than 83 characters (BIP173 limit), so bech32_decode fails the round-trip inside encode() and encode() returns None. /output/lib/bech32/codec.mjs bech32Decode() has no such check: after `const position = normalized.lastIndexOf(SEPARATOR)` it only tests `position < 1 || position + 1 + CHECKSUM_LENGTH > normalized.length`. It needs an additional rejection when the separator position (== hrp length) exceeds 83. Boundary is exact: hrp length 83 matches (both print aaaa...1pqypq6yea52), 84 diverges. Reproduces for every hrp length >= 84 tested (84..95, 200, 500, 1000), for every witness version (0, 1, 2, 16), every program length (2, 3, 20, 32, 40), both `--a <v>` and `--a=<v>` spellings, and for filler chars a/b/q/z/0/1/-/!/~ (any hrp made only of chars that are not uppercase letters; all-uppercase long hrps happen to agree because both sides already return None for mixed case). It is NOT a total-address-length rule: hrp=83 with a 40-byte program produces a 155-char address that both sides emit identically, so the port is right to omit the classic `len(bech) > 90` check.

result.notes:
Scope: --a (hrp) fuzzing only. 4507 differential case pairs across 7 generator runs (/tmp/hrp1.mjs, /tmp/hrp2.mjs, /tmp/hrp3.mjs, /tmp/hrp4b.mjs, /tmp/hrp5.mjs, /tmp/hrp6.mjs, /tmp/hrp7.mjs, /tmp/hrp8.mjs). Exactly one finding, and every single failure observed across all runs collapses to it (69/69 in the length grid, 12/12 in the random no-uppercase run, 6/6 in the argparse-edge run) — no second failure class appeared.

Covered and MATCHING (no differences):
- empty hrp: `--a ''` and `--a=` -> both "None".
- every ASCII char 0x20..0x7e as a 1-char hrp, in both `--a <ch>` and `--a=<ch>` spellings, with witver 0/1/5/16 and 20-/32-byte programs (285 cases). Also control chars 0x01,0x07-0x0d,0x1b,0x1f,0x7f (NUL is unpassable through execve).
- all 2-char combos over a 42-char interesting-ASCII alphabet (1764 cases).
- uppercase / mixed case: BC, Bc, bC, A..Z, AbCdEfGh, X1Y, full alphabet, plus I/i, K/k, S/s (case-folding traps) -> all "None" on both sides.
- hrp containing '1': '1', '11', '111', 'a1', '1a', 'a1b', 'bc1', 'bc11', '1b1c1', '1'*n -> all produce valid addresses identically (the separator is always the last '1' since '1' is not in CHARSET).
- hrp containing '=' and all other ASCII punctuation via `--a=<v>`.
- digit-only hrps: '0', '9', '0123456789', '1234567890'*3.
- leading '-': both `--a -1` and `--a=-1`, plus -12, -1.5, -b, '-', '--', and `--a` at end of argv (argparse "expected one argument" path) -> identical, including error text and exit code 2.
- non-ASCII: accented (e-acute, u-diaeresis, sharp-s, dotted/dotless I), CJK, hiragana, emoji + skin-tone ZWJ sequence, regional indicators, standalone and applied combining acute/diaeresis, Arabic/Hebrew letters, Arabic-Indic and mathematical digits, micro sign, ligatures, fullwidth forms, NBSP/thin space/ideographic space/ZWSP/BOM, U+FFFF, U+10FFFF -> all "None" on both sides, and the port's code-point (not UTF-16 unit) iteration in bech32HrpExpand matches.
- prefixes/suffixes of each other: b/bc/bcr/bcrt/bcrtx, t/tb/tbc, c/crt/rt, bcbc/bcbcbc with witver 0/1/16.
- 700 random printable-ASCII hrps len 1..90, 400 random no-uppercase-ASCII hrps len 1..83, 200 random ASCII+non-ASCII mixes.
- argparse edges involving --a: repeated --a (last wins), `--a=--b`, `--a --b`, missing --a, `-a`, `--A`, `--` terminator, whitespace-only and space-padded hrps.

Suspicious but unconfirmable: I cannot distinguish whether the reference's rule is literally `len(hrp) > 83` or `bech.rfind('1') > 83`, because the data alphabet CHARSET excludes '1', so the last '1' in a generated address is always at index len(hrp). Either formulation is a correct fix. Also note the reference in this build has NO 90-character total-address cap (155-char addresses encode fine), so a fix must add only the 83-char hrp bound, not the upstream pip `bech32` package's `len(bech) > 90` check.

mismatches.why: The reference bech32 build rejects any hrp longer than 83 characters (the BIP-173 HRP limit), so bech32.encode returns None. The port's bech32Decode in /output/lib/bech32/codec.mjs has no hrp-length guard, so the round-trip validation in segwit.mjs encode() succeeds and it prints the address. Boundary is exact and sharp: hrp length 83 -> address (both agree), hrp length 84 -> ref None / port address. Verified content-independent ('x'*84 and 'ab'*42 both None in ref) and program-length-independent (fails identically for --c of 2, 20, 32 and 40 bytes, i.e. total address lengths 96 through 172). Verified for every witver that would otherwise yield an address (0 with 20/32-byte programs, 1..16 with 2..40-byte programs); 100/768 cells failed in the witver -32..31 x hrplen {83,84,85} sweep, which is exactly the set of cells where a valid address would be produced. Note the guard must sit inside the decode round trip, not before bech32_encode: with hrp length 84 and --b 32 both binaries still raise IndexError from bech32_encode, so the length rejection happens strictly after encoding. Suggested fix: add `if (hrp.length > 83) return [null, null];` to bech32Decode (equivalently a `len(hrp) > 83` clause alongside the existing pos/checksum-length test).

- witver <= -33 or >= 32: IndexError from bech32_encode, exit 1, traceback on stderr, for every program length. (CHARSET[witver] is out of range; -32..-1 wrap via Python negative indexing.)

mismatches.why: Ordering bug. CPython's _parse_known_args classifies EVERY argv token by calling _parse_optional up front (building the 'OA' pattern string) before executing a single action, so the 'ambiguous option' error preempts everything. /output/lib/py/argparse.mjs parse_known_args (lines 149-206) only calls #parseOptional lazily as it walks left to right, so any earlier token that exits first hides the ambiguity. Two observable sub-cases: (a) help earlier in argv -> ref exit 2 ambiguous vs port exit 0 help ('-h --=x', '-h --=', '--help --=1', '-h --= --b x'); (b) a type-conversion error earlier in argv -> both exit 2 but different message: argv ['--b','notanint','--=x'] gives ref "error: ambiguous option: --=x could match --help, --a, --b, --c" vs port "error: argument --b: invalid int value: 'notanint'" (same for ['--b','x','--=']). '--=<anything>' is the only ambiguous token this parser can produce (the only common prefix of two long options is '--'). Cases that already agree: '--=x' alone, ['--=x','-h'], ['--a','--='], ['--','--=x'] (after '--' the scan stops classifying, so no error), ['--a','bc','--b','5','--c','x','--=1'].

- No hangs, no JS stack traces, no Node warnings anywhere. Worst case wall time: 130000-char hrp = 0.29s ref vs 0.57s port; 32700-element --c = 0.22s vs 0.28s; everything else under 0.3s on both sides.

Environment limit worth knowing (NOT a port bug): a single argv element cannot exceed MAX_ARG_STRLEN = 131072 bytes, so a 50000-element --c ("255," x 50000 = 200 KB) cannot be passed to either binary — execve fails with E2BIG before either program starts. The largest testable --c is ~32767 elements; I used 32700. Same cap limits hrp to ~131071 chars; I used 130000.
